answer: The algorithm computes a prime-length transform F_s from power-of-two transforms F_t, and the identity that does this (Sikusup, page roz) has the coordinate reindexings P_s and P_t inside it. The wiki says these reindexings are never run as sorts, and the pages I read do not spell out why a sort would be costly on the tape machine; they only say the usual implementation sorts twice on each coordinate, and that the cost accounting charges chunk exchanges. The target permutation Q disappears because the Divasov identity writes QF_t u as two pointwise chirp phases around one convolution of length T, and a convolution is computed by transforms and pointwise products, so Q is just part of a convolution and is never executed. The source permutation R disappears because each t_i is a unit modulo s_i, so R acts as a unit-multiplier reindexing R_beta on each axis, and F^+ R_beta = R_beta^{-1} F^+ (Nizizag, page zom). In (R F_s^+)[(R F_s u)(R F_s v)] the permutation R commutes with the pointwise product, so the expression becomes F_s^+ (F_s u . F_s v) with the two R factors gone, and the inverse-transform identity gives u*v/S^2. No sort is needed because the reindexing is absorbed algebraically (into a convolution for Q, and by commuting with the opposite transform for R), not executed. Confidence is moderate: I followed the algebra of the identities on pages zom, pap and roz, but I could not verify the cost reasons for avoiding sorts, and the key chirp and resampling identities are imported from cited literature.

key_idea.statement: The source and target coordinate permutations are never carried out: the target one becomes part of a chirp convolution, and the source one commutes through the transforms and cancels against itself, so the identity is kept as a formula rather than a sort.
